original_text:
Today I was reading about multi statements transactions feature in Databricks.

To be honest, I never really realized that databricks doesn't support multi table multi transactions and Franco Patano in his session at AI summit did mention that 70 to 80% of overall transactions are single table transactions only.

So, basically, if you are updating, deleting or inserting multiple tables in same transaction, either all should fail or all pass. Classic warehousing thing, BEGIN and COMMIT. 

Franco gave the classical example of star schema where you do need multi transaction support. You need to make sure that fact and dimensions both have the data.

So, this feature is in private preview right now.

Databricks uses optimistic concurrency where it never locks the table when multiple people read/write the table. It creates the snapshot for each transaction in such a way that there are no dirty reads for users doing different transactions at the same time on same table.

Only at the write time it sees that if any updates were made on the table, If there were changes, it'll get the updated records and then do it's own commit afterwards. It's like a git rebase.

Another cool feature is; concurrency is not at table or partition level; it is at the row level, in case if multiple transactions are updating the same row at same time, it'll retry and try to commit.
